status: FINAL. Frozen from its first dev run (controller pins the sha).
market: ES (traded as MES). Signal from the frozen bar['mtd'] (ES month-to-date same-contract return and 10y par-yield change, both as of the previous close) and bar['sessions_left_in_month'] (published NYSE holiday rule).
hypothesis: Near month-end, balanced funds rebalance toward fixed equity/bond weights: when ES has outrun Treasuries month-to-date they sell equities, when it has lagged they buy. So on the last sessions of the month, trading ES AGAINST the month-to-date equity-minus-bond return, 09:35 -> 15:55 with a 1:1 bracket of 0.5 x ATR20, beats random-direction trades on the same sessions with the same bracket.
mechanism: Calendar rebalancing by pensions/balanced funds is mechanical and predictable; the equity sale (purchase) needed is proportional to the drift of the equity weight, i.e. to equity minus bond return since the last rebalance (Harvey, Mazzoleni & Melone 2025). Their price pressure lowers (raises) equity returns over the days it is executed.

sources.summary: Harvey, Mazzoleni & Melone (2025, NBER WP 33554), 'The Unintended Consequences of Rebalancing': when stocks are overweight, funds sell stocks/buy bonds, and equity returns fall ~17 bps over the next day (bonds +3 bps); not explained by momentum, reversal or macro controls; rebalancing costs ~$16bn/yr (~8 bps).

Their EDHEC slides (read via pdftotext): signals from a simulated 60/40 portfolio of front E-mini S&P 500 and front 10y T-note futures; Distance_t = drift of the equity weight from 60%. Calendar signal = the drift since the last month-end reset; the regression Ret_{t+1} on Calendar_t x Dummy(last N days of month) uses 'week4': next-day S&P 500 coefficient -0.27 (s.e. 0.075), S&P minus 10y -0.30; Threshold signal -0.33. Daily futures data 1997-09-10 to 2023-03-17 (6,223 obs). Next-day return = close-to-close (includes the overnight).

Etula, Rinne, Suominen & Vaittinen (2020, RFS 33(1) 75-111), 'Dash for Cash': month-end institutional cash needs produce systematic price patterns (temporary rises in the cost of capital around key month-end dates; equity selling up to ~4 business days before month-end given settlement). Supports a last-week window; their exact equity return pattern was not read (full text not opened).

prior: Moderate for the existence of the effect, weak for this trade. HMM's sample covers 1997-2023, so ES dev 2011-18 AND val1/val2 up to 2023-03 are in-sample for them (no fresh-sample claim). Their effect is next-day close-to-close; this RTH 09:35 -> 15:55 leg misses the overnight. Their coefficient implies, for a typical 1% equity-weight drift (~4% equity-bond MTD gap), about -27 bps next day = ~0.25-0.35 of a 0.5 x ATR20 risk unit only for the large-drift months; typical months are a fraction of that. With ~280-460 trades the SE of mean R is ~0.045-0.06R, so twin p < 0.005 needs ~+0.13-0.17R net vs 0.069R cost: low power unless the effect is concentrated in large-drift months (config 2). Month-end ES drift (turn-of-month positive) is a known confound: side-matched twins handle direction mix, not a month-end-long drift interacting with a short-heavy signal (long share ~0.3).
overlap_with_closed: No closed family uses month-end calendar flows, rebalancing or bond-relative returns. Distinct from D1 (prior L-day own return, all days) by signal (equity minus bond MTD, a portfolio-weight drift, not own-return reversal), calendar gating (last 3-5 sessions only) and source; from close_auction (overnight last-30-min fade) and intraday momentum (same-day). The D1 row (daily reversal FAILED) is mild evidence only: a month-end subset of 'fade the prior move' overlaps D1's L5 signal on some days; disclosed, and the report gives the corr of the D2 side with D1-L5's side on the traded days.
timestamp_semantics: bar['mtd'] is as of the previous session's close (t-1): ret = c(t-1) / (c(base) moved onto t-1's contract) - 1, base = last listed session of the previous month; dy10 = UST10Y(t-1) - UST10Y(base), Treasury par yields fixed ~15:30 ET and published that evening. bar['sessions_left_in_month'] counts scheduled NYSE days after today by the published rule (ad hoc closures not anticipated). No data from today is used except the 09:30 bar close as the bracket centre.
features: X = mtd.ret - (-8 x mtd.dy10 / 100) = mtd.ret + 0.08 x mtd.dy10 (equity MTD return minus a 10y duration-8 bond return proxy, as in the plan); mtd None or dy10 None -> no trade
eligible = sessions_left_in_month <= N - 1 (the last N scheduled sessions of the month), N = 3 or 5

(config 2 only) z = X / (sd20 x sqrt(n)), sd20 = sample sd (n-1) of ret over the usable entries of hist[-20:] (ret not None, nyse_skipped == 0; >= 18 needed), n = number of hist entries with day > mtd.base_day (sessions in the MTD window); trade only if |z| >= 0.4307 (= the normal 1/3-2/3 quantile, i.e. the top and bottom terciles of a normal signal)

rules.bars: 5m RTH bars; decision on slot 0's close, market fill at the 09:35 open.
rules.sessions: skip NYSE half days and sessions without ATR20 (controller rule). Each eligible session is traded independently with that day's X (MTD updates daily).
rules.entry: side = -1 if X > 0 (equities ahead of bonds -> funds sell equities -> short), +1 if X < 0; X == 0 -> no trade. Config 2 additionally needs |z| >= 0.4307.
rules.risk: stop = c0 - side x 0.5 x ATR20, target = c0 + side x 0.5 x ATR20 (ATR20 = mean of the last 20 hist 'tr'). Controller-enforced.

grid_note: Neighbour chain (N3, any X) - (N5, any X) - (N5, |z| >= 0.43): each step changes one parameter.
deviation_from_plan: The plan's configs were X = 0 or top/bottom tercile x last 3 or last 1 sessions. The count-only scan shows (a) 'last 1 session' gives 92 dev trades (46 with the tercile) and 'tercile x last 3' 144, all below the frozen dev gate's 200-trade minimum, so they would fail by construction; (b) a trailing-history tercile restarts at each split's 60-day load window, giving 96 val1 trades (< the val minimum 100) by construction. So: last 5 sessions added (= HMM's 'week4' and Etula's ~4-business-days settlement window), last 1 dropped, and the tercile is the scale-free normal-tercile z cut (no long history). Rule shape (entry, bracket, k) unchanged.

Dev 2011-02..2018-12: (N3, any X) 279, long share 0.32; (N5, any X) 459, 0.34; (N5, |z| >= 0.43) 326, 0.30, every year 30-45. val1: 105 / 175 / 145. val2: 163 / 269 / 184. (The val counts were computed while checking the tercile design; they are counts of eligible signals, not outcomes.)
